Might have been helpful to preface the question with that bit of background. It's really easy to be mistaken for a troll when questioning why someone chooses PHP at all.

But to answer your question, I think it's because of how quickly it is to get up and running as well as how forgiving the language can be. There are easy ways to be very insecure by accident, such as using globals or storing passwords in plaintext. Without a framework or strongly-typed language to enforce certain standards (which is usually the case with Python/Ruby), it can cause problems. Whenever someone asks me what makes me think PHP is easier to get started on, I always ask them how many "Hello world" examples are there for PHP that don't require a framework, additional server modules as compared to other web languages (e.g., wsgi for Python, Unicorn for Ruby). That is my case-in-point, it's faster and less work to get a very basic PHP website up than it is for Python or Ruby. Almost all examples I've seen for those two languages are centered around frameworks.

In all the really "travely" places the benefits of a backpack far outweigh the benefits of a suitcase.

On a recent trip to Europe, then Africa, I did both. The total trip was over a month.

In Europe, my fiance (who is a bit prissy) and I went with large suitcases holding neatly packed and stylish clothes, a portable bluetooth speaker, a stylish hat for me, extra pairs of jeans, bottles of wine we wanted to take home, and of course my laptop. We did laundry at most once a week and never found ourselves running low on anything.

Then, off to Africa:. We left the big suitcases, laptop, and speaker in Europe at a hotel we'd use to layover. I switched to a backpack that had been stowed inside the suitcase and my fiance switched to a large carry-on. In Africa, it was all REI-style wicking clothes, Tide sink pods, and minimalism. I would do laundry every 3 days and leave quick-drying clothes out to dry in the sun.

Both served their function. To me, it's a question regarding the style of travel you're doing. If it's like camping in a hotel room, go with a backpack. If you're planning on some nicer dinners, if you're bringing back some bottles of wine, and if you don't want to look like a tourist in quick-dry "travel costume" clothes, suitcases are the only way to go.

I'd also add that I've never batted an eye at using a suitcase on a cobblestone street. They bounce around a little, but if you have a high-quality one with large, durable round wheels, it's a non-issue. Only cheap, shitty suitcases are phased.

Is it still safe to log in into my bank account? (url bar)

Looking at the encryption information that you can see by clicking the lock, they are using obsolete cryptography. If no one is monitoring your connection then you should still be fine, but know that it isn't as secure as other methods.
New versions of chrome have made older modes of encryption obsolete rendering the SSL you're seeing above. I think Farseli has it said pretty well.

It could be caused by a number of issues. The bank's security certificate could have been generated by a non-authoritative entity, or your connection could be being decrypted along the way. I certainly would exercise caution. * Have you ever used it before and noted that it had a green lock icon up there before today? If so - I would not use it. * I would also question the overall security of the bank if they're not paying for an authority to issue their certificates - they're really not that expensive so there's no reason not to. But if they generate their own unsigned certificate then, well, this could be perfectly secure connection as well. * If the latter case I mentioned is the reasoning - are you at work or on a network you typically don't use? I'd probably not use it. * The worst case here is that you are being subject to a MITM (Man-in-the-Middle) attack and someone has captured your traffic on its path to the bank site in hopes of stealing your access credentials and bank account info. Generally caused by malware on your system and/or being on a public/open network.

If you want to do a quick test - maybe use a smartphone that is on your 4G (or other network not the same WiFi network as the one your computer is on currently). If the site loads with a green lock there but not from your computer I would suspect a network based compromise or malware and say MITM attack is in play for sure at that point. But regardless I would probably email or call your bank and talk to them about it.
Okay it was a red lock on my phone. It's the probably the website then.
If you click on the lock and it's a problem with the level of encryption, yes, you're safe. If it's a problem with the certificate, no, it's not.
